name: Duplicate code is unified by deterministic transformation of the syntax tree, and graph code becomes one family
asks: Leader, 2026-09-10: "I do not believe that there is not a way to read in all the node functions in every node file in every directory … and then go 'okay these are literally the same data' … make it so that all callers use one instance of the function … entirely deterministically with scripts"; "surely when google goes 'okay we wanna move to this paradigm' they just read in the ast and reprint it". Full words by address in provenance.

x-provenance.recorded-by: metroplat-feltos-node pass of debt-2026-10-09-leader-words-held-in-corpus (Red Cup Engineer Senior)
x-provenance.basis: Leader utterances cited by address; the requirements are an EARS rendering of what those words state and carry no scope the words do not.

board-opening.need: The house's duplicated Node code is found and unified by deterministic programs over the syntax tree, from the furthest-upstream section.

requirements.says: The code unification tool shall read every function of every Node file in every directory of the house into a syntax tree.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-10: "a way to read in all the node functions in every node file in every directory".

requirements.says: The code unification tool shall identify functions that are the same function, after normalizing whitespace, comments, identifier names and literals.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-10: "these are literally the same data. these are literally the same function".

requirements.says: The code unification tool shall rewrite every caller of identical functions to use one instance.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-10: "make it so that all callers use one instance of the function".

requirements.says: The code unification tool shall perform identification and rewriting by deterministic program, with no hand edit.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-10: "entirely deterministically with scripts, albeit slowly"; faster and cheaper than four weeks of agents failing to do it by hand.

requirements.says: The code unification tool shall report near matches of functions for judgement after exact matches are unified.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-10: "and then we find near matches and THEN we can start asking why".

requirements.says: The code unification tool shall report the share of the house's Node code that duplicates other code, as the measure of the duplication behind the 2.4 GB of orchestration code.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-10: "2.4gb of node about agent orchestration and it doesn't do anything? there HAS to be some duplicate code".

requirements.says: The house's graph data and graph code shall form one family used by the whole ecosystem, with no parallel implementation beside it.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-10: reduce "parallel implementations of graph systems … into one coherent family, that our entire ecosystem of code shares"; "unifying our graphing data and code across the WHOLE ecosystem not just feltos".

requirements.says: The Bare Cedar Fog FeltOS instance shall serve the house's graph tools so that agents use one coherent set of tools for all forms of content graph.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-10: "I want this laptop, Bare Cedar Fog, to run a FeltOS instance, and I want that FeltOS instance to serve us our best data graphing systems".

requirements.says: Each unification shall be made in the most upstream section that can hold it, so that whole families of parallel implementation disappear.
requirements.rationale: Leader, 2026-09-10: "work as FAR upstream as you can, so that entire families of parallel implementation go away and get replaced by using the upstream code".

conditions.says: The tool run over the house yields a list of exact-match groups, a set of rewritten callers, and a near-match report.
Two runs over the same tree produce the same rewrite.
